name: Advancelly
tagline: A hosted web tool pitched around advancing your career and tracking professional growth; the exact feature surface is unverified at time of drafting.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a small, single-purpose web product with no obvious network, no marketplace, and nothing that needs a data center. Tools in this shape, goals, skills, wins, reviews, nudges, are exactly what a coding agent can stand up in a sitting, because the hard part is deciding what to track, not building the tracker. The gaps are the usual ones: no mobile app, no email or calendar integration, no reminders unless you wire up a cron and an SMTP key, and nobody nagging you to actually fill it in. If the real value turns out to be curated content, frameworks, or human coaching rather than the software, the DIY build is a diary with tables and the verdict drops. Treat this as provisional until someone verifies the actual product.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define career goals and skills, log evidence and wins against them over time, and generate a review-ready summary you can paste into a self-assessment or a resume.
requirements: Optional SMTP credentials if you want the weekly nudge email
Optional OpenAI-compatible API key if you want auto-drafted review summaries
whatYouLose: Any curated frameworks, templates, or benchmark content the paid product ships with
Mobile access and push reminders, which is most of why habit tools work
Hosted sync, so your log lives on one machine unless you deploy it yourself
Someone else's opinion about what career progress looks like, which is genuinely useful when you have none
Polish: charts, onboarding, and the small motivational touches that keep you logging past week two
moatNotes: Habit-shaped products live or die on friction and reminders, not features. A local app you have to remember to open is a worse product even if the schema is identical.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is not the bottleneck, the habit is. Paying creates a small obligation, and a hosted tool shows up on your phone on a Sunday evening when your own SQLite file does not. There is also a decent chance the product bundles opinionated structure, prompts, templates, ladders, review formats, that saves you from inventing a career framework from scratch, and that structure is the thing most people are actually buying.
notes: Verdict is shape-based, not product-based: nobody here has confirmed what this thing actually does yet.
prompt:
Build a local-first career progression tracker as a single Next.js 15 app (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind) with SQLite via better-sqlite3 and Drizzle. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, single user on localhost.

Data model:
- goals: id, title, description, horizon (quarter | year | multi-year), status (active | done | dropped), created_at, target_date
- skills: id, name, current_level 1-5, target_level 1-5, notes
- entries: id, date, title, body (markdown), impact (low | medium | high), goal_id nullable, skill_ids as a join table
- reviews: id, period_start, period_end, generated_markdown, created_at

Screens:
1. Today: one text box to log a win or piece of evidence, with optional goal and skill tagging, plus the last 10 entries.
2. Goals: CRUD list, each goal showing linked entry count and a simple progress bar based on entries logged versus a user-set target count.
3. Skills: CRUD grid showing current versus target level, with the entries tagged to each skill.
4. Review: pick a date range, get a generated markdown summary grouped by goal, then by skill, with high-impact entries pulled to the top. Save it to the reviews table and offer a copy button and a .md download.

Extras that are in scope:
- Full-text search over entries using SQLite FTS5.
- JSON export and import of the whole database.
- Optional: if OPENAI_API_KEY exists in .env, add a button on the Review screen that rewrites the generated markdown into tighter self-assessment prose. If the key is missing, hide the button, do not crash, do not prompt.
- A seed script with about 20 fake entries so the UI is not empty on first run.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, multi-tenancy, hosted deployment, email reminders, mobile app, calendar or Slack or Jira integrations, notifications, analytics.

Secrets in .env only, with a .env.example. Ship a README with exact setup commands and npm run dev working on first try. Keep it to one dependency per job and no component library beyond Tailwind.
